newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian maize, wheat futures extend advance.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian maize, wheat futures extend advance.

text.p: Speculative purchases on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued to drive up wheat and maize futures prices on Thursday.
Both have has been firming for the past three weeks following a slump in prices because of surplus stocks, traders said.
They said prices on the physical markets were higher than futures, but the rising trend on the BCE was not justified by market fundamentals.

"Prices should go down, but one or two brokerages are buying milling wheat aggressively and the smaller ones are following," said Swap Ugynoki Kft's Imre Uzonyi. "A collapse is certain to come, and whoever closes positions quickly will take profits."
Almost all milling wheat and feed wheat maturities traded on Thursday rose by the daily limit of 400 forints per tonne while maize futures firmed by 200 to 350 forints.
The most actively traded milling wheat maturity, August, finished up by 400 forints at 21,240 on 206 lots, while May wheat rose 400 forints on 180 lots to end at 25,100.
July maize closed at 18,000, up 400, on a total volume of 250 lots.
Traders said they did not a see real opportunity for the sale of surplus wheat and maize stocks.
Bulgarian buying interest was not promising due to the uncertain finances of buyers in the country, while Serb purchases were likely to be limited to small amounts.
